added.name: Evardi
added.long_description: At least 94% of US outage minutes start on the distribution grid, and most utilities are blind between the substation and the meter. Evardi builds a live model of a utility’s network from data it already has, matching every meter to its transformer and using virtual meters to show load and solar on every transformer. On top of that model, our AI agents do the engineering work utilities need at the grid edge: checking switching orders, finding outages after extreme weather and planning for new load from DERs and data centers. Because the model sees every transformer, it will also help utilities decide when new wires are really needed, and how distribution load can free up transmission for new data centers. We’re working with utilities across the globe that together serve over 10 million customers.
added.one_liner: Agents that engineer the grid edge

added.name: Ailit
added.long_description:
Ailit is building the electric energy system for North American freight rail. Our first product, Superwagon, is a battery wagon designed to power existing diesel-electric locomotives, allowing railroads to electrify the fleets they already own.

Superwagon carries swappable battery packs that supply electricity to the locomotive’s existing electric motors. Discharged packs are exchanged for charged ones along the route and recharged off-board, providing operators with limitless range.

We deliver energy as a service, owning and operating the batteries and swapping sites. Railroads pay for energy with no upfront equipment purchase, with pricing set at 20% below today’s diesel cost.

Founded in Stockholm by Christian Lind and Emil Tagesson, our team is now based in San Francisco. We’re building our first full-scale prototype and targeting first deployment in summer 2027.
added.one_liner: Electrifying North American freight rail with swappable batteries.
